name: GemStone/S
tagline: Smalltalk object database where application code runs inside the transactional object repository.
description: GemStone/S is an object database and Smalltalk application server: objects persist in a shared, transactional repository, and methods execute inside the database in Gem processes, so code and data live together without a mapping layer. GemStone/S 64 Bit supports very large repositories, a shared page cache across many sessions, optimistic and pessimistic concurrency, and hot standby. It underpins long-running financial, shipping and logistics systems and the open-source Seaside web stack (GLASS). GemTalk Systems still ships regular releases, and a free Community licence makes it easy to try.

pricing.notes: Free Community licence with limits; enterprise licences quoted by system size.

scale.notes: Many sessions share one repository via a shared page cache; hot standby for failover.

strengths: Code runs next to persistent objects, so there is no ORM or network round-trip per object
Mature transactional engine with decades of production use
Class versioning lets schemas evolve on live systems
Regular releases from an active vendor and a free Community licence
weaknesses: Requires Smalltalk skills, which are scarce
Limited interoperability with mainstream data tooling
useCases: Long-lived Smalltalk business systems in finance and logistics
